scope: Fixed 504-update boundary-weighted head. Compare original neural fields with neural-seeded and RGB-clustered paper palettes using the existing illumination-aware mixture helper. All 16 real training photos and 96 synthetic original/scene/printed views scored at 320; same 32 source-separated development photos reviewed at source-resolution colour classification. Body, model, annotations and source/crop data unchanged. No training, per-photo winners or deployment.

native.review: Both palette methods restore the stacked-heart structure, shaded red/gold checker, fine web joins, nativity figures, dragonfly wings and sharper star rays. RGB clustering also recovers the blue/red printed-tree checker that neural-selected colours classify by ink. Other printed stripes/dots/flowers still become false cuts. RGB clustering loses the blue printed heart held in a hand by separating the hand instead of its papers. Neither fixes frozen body omissions on the house and candlestick.

interpretation: Colour calibration sharpens boundaries compared with raw neural fields, but learned palette selection does not beat the RGB-cluster control consistently. The fixed-crop pipeline gives 11/32 checked derived-mask pairs for learned palettes versus 13/32 for RGB, with no learned-only checked gains. Printed interiors remain confused, fixed crop failures remain, and small mask changes can alter count scheduling. No full boundary ground truth exists for this development cohort.
next: Improve count-shortlist stability and body localization before more material-head training. Do not deploy this candidate or interpret agreement with its own mask as original-artwork recovery.
